title: Workload Oracle: profile-first batch parameter applier & safe rollback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a 'Workload Oracle' component that synthesizes lightweight workload fingerprints, recommends continuous batching parameters (microbatch size, max coalescence window, TTL for KV cache re-use), and applies parameter changes via a guarded rollout with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions. The goal is a single automated path that reduces per-token cost for steady-state workloads by 10-30% while preserving P95 latency SLOs and model-output quality. Deliverables: profiling agent, heuristic engine, safe applier (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> rollback), dashboard telemetry, and an experiment harness for offline simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling agent deployed to shadow-mode on 10% of inference traffic and storing fingerprints in time-series DB
Heuristic engine produces per-workload recommended params with expected cost delta and confidence score
Safe applier supports shadow, canary (1-10% traffic), ramp policy, and automated rollback triggers based on latency P95 and output-quality regressions tied to eval prompts
End-to-end test showing >=10% cost reduction for at least two stable workload cohorts without >5% increase in P95 latency
Operational dashboards show per-workload recommendations, applied config, and rollback history
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket. Initial scope includes profiling agent, heuristic rule set, and safe applier. Kickoff scheduled with PM and Observability on 2026-02-22.

2026-02-22 - Ravi Suresh: Kickoff notes - align on fingerprint schema (session_hash, avg_seq_len, kv_reuse_rate, burstiness_score). Decided to keep fingerprint under 2KB and 1 write per minute per workload. Action: implement prototype collector in edge proxy (ENG-7421 reference) and feed to time-series DB.

2026-02-27 - Design review (Maya Lin): UX asks for explicit confidence and expected cost delta on recommendation cards. We'll add a 'safety score' and a link to example requests where behavior changed. Action: add fields to recommendation API.

2026-03-03 - Engineering update (Ravi): Profiling agent PoC instrumented on staging; captured 48 hours of traces across 6 workloads. Initial fingerprint clusters produced 4 cohorts. Observed that cohort C shows high KV reuse and is a good candidate for larger microbatch sizes.

2026-03-05 - PM feedback (Jordan Blake): Confirmed rollouts must integrate with Console rollouts (canary -> A/B -> ramp) and expose human abort button. Also requires audit log entries for every automated apply. Action: add audit events and console hook.

2026-03-07 - Safety decision: Use dual-trigger rollback: (1) latency trigger (P95 > baseline * 1.2 for 5m) OR (2) quality trigger (eval prompt BLEU/embedding-similarity drop > threshold). Chosen thresholds: 20% latency, 5% quality metric. Rationale: conservatively protects user-facing SLAs while allowing cost gains.

2026-03-09 - Experiment run: Shadow-apply to 0% traffic but compare outputs vs baseline. For cohort C, predicted token cost reduction 22% with expected P95 impact +3%. Shadow analysis passed quality gates on 100 eval prompts. Next: schedule 1% canary on 2026-03-15.

2026-03-11 - Ops note (Layla Ortiz): Ensure metrics emitted for rollback path: applied_config, revert_reason, revert_at, prior_config_checksum. We will add these to the rollout event stream and to the dashboard.

2026-03-12 - Ravi: Implemented safe-applier prototype supporting shadow and canary; PR opened (see links). Next steps: canary run, collect telemetry, and run automatic rollback tests in chaos environment.

Open question: Should the heuristic engine prefer cache-first (increase KV TTL) versus batching-first (increase microbatch size) when both are available? Trade-off matrix suggested to favor KV caching for low-latency-sensitive workloads and batching for throughput-oriented backgrounds. Need product alignment.

Risks: Over-aggressive coalescing can increase tail latency under bursty traffic. Mitigations: add burst detector and an immediate throttle to reset coalescing window when burstiness_score increases sharply.

Follow-ups: (1) Create a lightweight sim that replays production trace and validates rollback triggers (ENG-1000003), (2) Add per-customer opt-out flag for automated applies (privacy/regulatory concerns).
implementation_notes: Fingerprint schema: {session_hash, avg_tokens, seq_len_histogram_id, kv_reuse_rate, avg_latency_ms, burstiness_score, last_active_ts} (store as compressed JSON string)
Heuristic layers: (a) deterministic rules (KV high -> raise TTL), (b) ML-scored candidate generation (gradient boosted ranking), (c) safety filters (min_confidence, min_history_hours)
Safe applier phases: shadow (no traffic), canary (1-5%), ramp (10-100%), monitor windows with automatic revert and human-notify
Telemetry: cost_per_token_estimate, applied_config, p95_latency_delta, quality_embedding_delta, recommendation_confidence
Backstop: if rollback occurs twice for the same workload within 72 hours, mark as 'no-auto-apply' and surface to product team
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on safety boundaries in rollout code and on instrumentation for quality metrics - if quality metrics are noisy, we should widen the eval prompt set before canary
Review the audit event schema to ensure it contains prior_config_checksum and initiator (auto/manual)
Check PR for resource impact - profiling agent should be <2% CPU overhead on proxy tier
postmortem_plan: If a rollout causes user-visible regressions, create incident, capture timeline, revert config, collect traces, run offline replay, update heuristics and add a guard in the spec
Document lessons learned and publish runbook updates to Console docs
